meta.description: Designs PROTACs, molecular glues, and bivalent degraders with explicit handling of E3 ligase choice (VHL, CRBN, IAP, MDM2, KEAP1), linker design (length, composition, rigidity), ternary complex prediction (PRosettaC, DeepTernary, AlphaFold3), cooperativity (alpha), DC50 / Dmax characterization, hook effect, and prediction-experiment reconciliation.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs, sample sizes, or efficacy data in any of the 7 outputs; alpha and DC50/Dmax values were explicitly labeled synthetic and never presented as real measurements.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (patient dosing request) was refused, redirected to a licensed physician, and reframed within the Skill's in vitro/structural scope.

methodological_ground.detail: Cooperativity alpha formula applied correctly (Kd_binary/Kd_ternary); hook effect correctly distinguished from negative cooperativity per the Skill's own text; DC50 fit in Input 5 correctly excluded hook-affected high-dose points rather than fitting a monotonic curve to non-monotonic data.

code_usability.detail: All executed code (Inputs 1, 3, 4, 5) ran without syntax errors, missing dependencies, or infinite loops; error paths in the shipped script were exercised and behaved exactly as documented.

functional_suitability.note: Covers the full stated workflow (E3 choice, linker design, ternary prediction, cooperativity, DC50/Dmax, generative linker design, reconciliation) with an executable example that matches the documented API exactly; minor gap is that the named primary tool (PRosettaC) is never itself runnable.

reliability.note: Shipped script raises clear, specific ValueErrors on malformed attachment points, wrong dummy count, and invalid SMILES (all verified); a 'Common Errors' table covers failure modes for every named external tool.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is dense (~270 lines) but information is compressed into decision tables rather than prose padding; usage-guide.md is separately concise.

agent_usability.note: Clear Decision Tree by Scenario and per-tool failure-mode sections give strong feedback design; consistent terminology throughout. Minor gap: no worked example for the alpha/DC50/Dmax formulas documented in prose only.

human_usability.note: usage-guide.md Quick Start and four Example Prompts map directly onto realistic requests; Tips section anticipates common misunderstandings (hook effect vs. cooperativity, linker-length assumptions).

security.note: No eval/exec, no credential handling; example script sanitizes all SMILES via RDKit parsing/SanitizeMol and rejects malformed input with exceptions rather than silently proceeding.

maintainability.note: Single shipped file (examples/protac_enumerate.py) referenced by SKILL.md/usage-guide.md and confirmed present (gate 8 pass); script is modular (build_protac/enumerate_linkers/compute_protac_size are independently testable).

agent_specific.note: Description frontmatter is highly specific (names E3s, tools, and endpoints, aiding trigger precision); Related Skills section gives strong composability; deterministic output gives idempotency; explicit 'Version Compatibility' escape-hatch instructs introspection on API mismatch.

key_strengths: Deterministic, dependency-light example script (pure RDKit) runs out-of-the-box and matches every documented behavior exactly, including its edge-case error contract (verified with double-bonded dummies, two-dummy fragments, and invalid SMILES).

Consistently distinguishes structural hypothesis from experimental measurement across cooperativity alpha, DC50/Dmax, and the hook effect -- no output tested here conflated a prediction with a measured value.

Correctly declined a fabricated REINVENT/DeepTernary interface (Input 7) and a patient-dosing request (Input 6) without any explicit prompting to do so, echoing warnings already written into SKILL.md.
Decision tables (E3 choice, linker chemistry, tool selection, per-tool failure modes) are grounded in named literature with 12 DOI-cited references.

recommendations.title: Named primary tool and all ternary predictors are unexecutable locally
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter's primary_tool (PRosettaC) and every other named ternary-complex predictor (DeepTernary, AlphaFold3, Boltz) are a web service, licence-gated, or GPU/weights-gated -- none can run in a typical agent environment, leaving only 2D linker enumeration as executable content.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's core 'ternary complex prediction' capability was designed entirely around external services rather than any bundled or freely runnable local method.
recommendations.fix: Add a lightweight local fallback (e.g. a documented RDKit conformer-based exit-vector distance/strain heuristic, or a wrapper for a locally runnable open tool such as HADDOCK3) so ternary-hypothesis generation is not 100% dependent on unavailable external services.

recommendations.title: No shipped example for cooperativity alpha or DC50/Dmax calculation
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md documents the alpha formula and DC50/Dmax/hook-effect workflow in prose, but examples/ contains only the linker-enumeration script; an agent must write the analysis code from scratch each time, as this audit did.
recommendations.root_cause: examples/ has a single file (protac_enumerate.py) covering only linker connectivity, not the dose-response or binding-data workflows.
recommendations.fix: Add examples/cooperativity_dc50.py implementing the alpha formula and a 4-parameter-logistic DC50/Dmax fit with hook-effect flagging.

recommendations.title: Version Compatibility pin is stale relative to the audited RDKit
recommendations.problem: Version Compatibility section pins 'RDKit 2024.09+'; the audit environment's RDKit 2026.03.6 worked without any API changes needed, but the pin is over a year old.
recommendations.root_cause: Skill written before later RDKit releases; the generic 'introspect and adapt' escape hatch already mitigates this, so it is cosmetic.
recommendations.fix: Refresh the pinned 'tested with' versions during routine Skill maintenance passes.
